[[Chengdu Tiancheng F.C.|Chengdu Blades]] |relegated = [[Nanjing Yoyo F.C.|Nanjing Yoyo]] |biggest home win= {{nowrap|[[Guangzhou F.C.|Guangzhou]] 10–0 [[Nanjing Yoyo F.C.|Nanjing]] (21 July)}} |biggest away win= {{nowrap|[[Nanjing Yoyo F.C.|Nanjing]] 0–5 [[Guangzhou F.C.|Guangzhou]] (23 October)}} |highest scoring = {{nowrap|[[Guangzhou F.C.|Guangzhou]] 10–0 [[Nanjing Yoyo F.C.|Nanjing]] (21 July)}} |league topscorer= [[Gao Lin]] (20 goals) |matches = 156 |total goals = 381 |prevseason = [[2009 China League One|2009]] |nextseason = [[2011 China League One|2011]] }} The '''2010 [[China League One]]''' was the seventh season of the league since the establishment. ==Teams== After [[2009 in Chinese football|2009 season]], [[Liaoning F.C.|Liaoning Whowin]] and [[Shanghai Shenxin F.C.|Nanchang Bayi Hengyuan]] were promoted to [[2010 Chinese Super League]] and [[Sichuan F.C.|Sichuan]] were relegated to [[2010 China League Two]]. They were replaced by [[Hunan Billows F.C.|Hunan Billows]] and [[Wuhan Yangtze River F.C.|Hubei Luyin]] which were promoted from [[2009 China League Two]], [[Chengdu Tiancheng F.C.|Chengdu Blades]] and [[Guangzhou F.C.|Guangzhou Evergrande]] who were relegated from [[2009 Chinese Super League]]. [[Beijing Sport University F.C.|Beijing Baxy&Shengshi]] took over [[Beijing Hongdeng F.C.|Beijing Hongdeng]] and take their position within the division.[https://sports.sohu.com/20100202/n270004204.shtml 北京宏登队同意转让 北京八喜队借“壳”战中甲] Chengdu Blades and Guangzhou Evergrande, who finished in 7th and 9th place in Super League 2009, were relegated from the top flight for [[2003–2009 Chinese football match-fixing scandals|match-fixing scandals]],[https://web.archive.org/web/20121108082639/http://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid=1172760.html Chengdu Blades demoted] while [[Qingdao Hailifeng F.C.|Qingdao Hailifeng]], who finished in 10th place in [[2009 China League One]], were banned from all future national matches organized by the [[Chinese Football Association|CFA]] for the same reason.[http://www.shanghaidaily.com/sp/article/2010/201002/20100222/article_429155.htm Relegations; ban handed to soccer's big fixers] On 21 July 2010, Guangzhou Evergrande trounced [[Nanjing Yoyo F.C.|Nanjing Yoyo]] 10-0 at [[Century Lotus Stadium]], setting a new record in Chinese professional football league for biggest ever league win in the process.[https://sports.sina.com.cn/j/2010-07-21/19005115192.shtml 恒大创造中国职业联赛最大分差 破单场净胜球纪录]{{in lang|zh}} On 25 September 2010, Guangzhou Evergrande and Chengdu Blades were promoted to the [[Chinese Super League]] for the [[2011 Chinese Super League|2011 season]] after Hubei Luyin draw 1-1 with [[Shanghai Zobon F.C.|Shanghai Zobon]].[https://sports.sina.com.cn/b/2010-09-25/18235218809.shtml 中甲恒大成都双双取胜 两队携手提前三轮重返中超]{{in lang|zh}} On 23 October, Nanjing Yoyo were relegated to [[China League Two]] for the [[2011 China League Two|2011 season]] after a 5-0 home defeat to Guangzhou
